title: Minus one, then AND
hook: Subtract 1, AND the two, and repeat until x is 0. What does the count of repeats measure?

knows: bit masks keep or clear named bits (mask-the-flags)
doesNotKnow: that x & (x - 1) removes exactly the lowest set bit, so it counts ones and tests powers of two

misconception: Subtracting 1 changes only the last digit, as in decimal.
objective: The learner can explain that x - 1 turns the lowest 1 bit into 0 and the zeros below it into 1s, so x & (x - 1) clears exactly that bit; repeating it until 0 counts the 1 bits (10110 takes 3), and x > 0 is a power of two exactly when one repeat gives 0.

claims.text: Repeating x = x & (x - 1) on 10110 gives 10100, then 10000, then 0: 3 repeats, one per 1 bit.
claims.source: Demo.tsx repeatsToZero(0b10110) and the stage's apply(); builder re-ran in Node (2026-10-14): 10110 -> 10100 -> 10000 -> 0. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. Node: 10110 -> 10100 -> 10000 -> 0, 3 repeats.

claims.text: Minus 1 is not a last-digit change: 10100 - 1 = 10011, three digits flipped. The lowest 1 becomes 0 and every 0 below it becomes 1, so the AND keeps only the bits the two share and clears that one bit.
claims.source: Write x = w1 0...0 (k trailing zeros). Then x - 1 = w0 1...1: bits above the lowest 1 are unchanged, so x & (x - 1) = w0 0...0. Node (v2, 2026-10-14): (20 - 1).toString(2) = '10011'; 10100 and 10011 differ in the last three digits. 10100 is the value the learner's first press produces from 10110 (milestone one-clear). | FC pass 24 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Own node (fc24/clr.mjs): (20 - 1).toString(2) = '10011'; 10100 vs 10011 differ in 3 digits. Reveal quotes startRun.chain[1], which is always 10100 (the run from 10110 is deterministic; fallback is the same constant). For x = 1..2^20: x XOR (x - 1) = 2^(lowest+1) - 1 (the lowest 1 and every 0 below it flip, nothing above) and x & (x - 1) = x - lowbit(x), 0 failures. Green marks (i <= lowest) match.

claims.text: 11111111 (255) takes 8 repeats to reach 0, one per 1 bit.
claims.source: Demo.tsx chainFrom(255) has 9 entries (8 repeats); 255 has eight 1 bits. Reached by 'Run from 11111111' (milestone long-run) and listed in the stage's finished-runs list. Builder's Node run, 2026-10-14. | FC pass 24 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Own node: chainFrom(255) has 9 entries, 8 repeats; popcount 8. For x = 1..2^20 repeats = popcount, 0 failures. Reveal names 11111111 only when it is the longest recorded run (milestone long-run needs 5+ repeats), quoting its own count.

claims.text: 10000 has one 1 bit and one repeat takes it to 0; x > 0 is a power of two exactly when one repeat of x & (x - 1) gives 0.
claims.source: x & (x - 1) clears only the lowest 1 bit (c2), so the result is 0 iff x had exactly one 1 bit, i.e. x is a power of two. Demo.tsx chainFrom(16) = [16, 0]; the stage labels such runs '(power of two)'. Builder checked x & (x - 1) === 0 against Number.isInteger(Math.log2(x)) for x = 1..4999 in Node, 2026-10-14. The v1 sentence about 2^30 and right shifts is dropped. | FC pass 24 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Own node: chainFrom(16) = [16, 0]; for x = 1..2^20, (x & (x - 1)) === 0 iff log2(x) is an integer, 0 failures. Runs list labels chain length 2 '(power of two)'; reveal quotes the first non-10110 one-repeat run with its own start (always one 1 bit, so true for any learner-toggled power of two).

recall.question: x is a positive whole number and x & (x − 1) equals 0. What do you know about x?
options: x is a power of two
x is 1 less than a power of two
recall.why: x & (x − 1) clears only the lowest 1 bit. Getting 0 means that was the only 1 bit, so x is a power of two.
